messages:
Sanjay: FYI — saw a spike in Xid 13/31 events across gpool-us-west-2 between 02:15-03:20 UTC. Cluster telemetry shows a ~3x increase vs baseline. Suspect a driver+firmware combination regression. Opening thread to plan validation before we push the driver+kernel roll next week.
Maria: Ugh. Any card IDs or node list?
Sanjay: Quick summary from last night's scrape: ops-bot reported increased `gpu_xid_errors_total` on nodes gpu-n-10..gpu-n-14. ECC correctable errors also up slightly. I'll paste the snippet I used:
```
# prometheus
sum(rate(gpu_xid_errors_total[1h])) by (node)
```
Maria: Good. Let's not mass-upgrade without a canary. Suggest a validation matrix: driver versions (525.x, 535.x), firmware revisions (v4.2, v4.4), kernel flavors (5.15, 6.1) — test all combos on a small canary pool.
Ryan: I can wire up a synthetic job harness that runs our micro-bench loop + long-tail text gen to exercise the KV cache and memory hot paths. Will run steady-state 6h runs.
Kevin: Also include stress tests that trigger ECC soft/hard errors simulation if possible. We should capture dmesg Xid logs and nvml reports for repro.
Emily: Reminder: draining nodes will reduce available GPU capacity ~20% for the night. Need to coordinate with capacity owners and maybe shift low-priority batch jobs. Ops scheduler might need a temporary cap bump.
ops-bot: ALERT SUMMARY: 2026-01-15T02:18Z - Xid spike on gpool-us-west-2. Affected nodes: gpu-n-10,gpu-n-11,gpu-n-12,gpu-n-13,gpu-n-14. Current pool utilization 68%.
Sanjay: Proposed plan:
- Canary group: 4 nodes in us-west-2 (gpu-n-20..gpu-n-23) with identical hardware mix.
- Test matrix: run combos Maria suggested for 6h each.
- Metrics to gate on: Xid rate per GPU (<0.1/hr), ECC correctable/unrecoverable delta (<10% above baseline), kernel oops/panic count == 0, SM utilization anomaly rate.
- Rollout window: 02:00-06:00 UTC next Tue night.
- Rollback triggers: any unrecoverable ECC, Xid rate > 1/hr on >1 card, or job failures > 2%.
Maria: Sounds good. Add collection of per-GPU nvml logs and `dmesg | grep NVRM` dumps to the test harness artifacts. We need a reproducible artifact to send to driver vendor if needed.
Ryan: I'll create a job in ci-infra: `ci/gpu-driver-validate` that spins up canary nodes, applies driver+fw combo via our imaging playbooks, runs harness, and uploads artifacts to 
https://redwood.internal/sre/gpu-validation/runs (will post link when done).
Kevin: For kernel testing, use our patched 6.1-rt branch and vanilla 5.15. Keep kernel configs constant except for the module stack. Also test with IOMMU on/off — previous flaky cards showed IOMMU-related Xids in older drivers.
Emily: Ops impact: we should prebook Reserved capacity for that window or mark some on-demand nodes as spare. Cost estimate: ~4 extra on-demand gpus for the 4h window ~ $240. Approve?
Sanjay: Approve cost. Also: schedule a preflight health-check 24h before the rollout to ensure no drift.
deploy-bot: Job queued: `ci/gpu-driver-validate` #389 by Ryan — estimated run time 8h.
Maria: Add a small canary that runs production traffic routing through canary model endpoint for 30m to catch edge-case latency regressions / OOMs. Use shadow traffic at 0.5%.
Ryan: Ack. I'll add a shadow route and synthetic traffic generator. Artifacts will include per-request latency and OOM traces.
Kevin: One more idea — run a kernel module stress loop (openmp memcopy + concurrent cuda launches) to try to trigger timing-related Xids. If it reproduces, we can binary-search which component triggers it.
Sanjay: Ownership:
- Canary run orchestration: Ryan
- Telemetry & gating dashboards: Maria
- Rollout coordination + capacity: Emily
- Postmortem & vendor escalation: Kevin
I'll post the final run checklist and link to the imaging playbook.
Maria: Checklist item: ensure `gpu_health_exporter` metrics are scraped at 15s for the canary. Increase retention for those runs to 90d.
Ryan: Started the first canary provisioning now (nodes gpu-n-20..23). ETA ~20m.
ops-bot: Notice: draining node gpu-n-20 for maintenance. Use `kubectl drain gpu-n-20 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
Emily: Reminder to set pod disruption budgets for high-priority workloads before you drain.
Sanjay: After first 6h canary run: initial results — driver 535.12 + fw v4.4 on kernel 6.1 showed reduced Xid rate (0.02/hr) vs baseline (0.08/hr). One ECC correctable spike on gpu-n-21 but cleared. I'll upload artifacts in a bit.
Maria: Prom graphs look promising. Can we run a longer 24h run on the successful combo before broad rollout?
Kevin: Yes — also get nvram and nvflash version checks. If stable for 24h, then plan staged rollout by region (us-west -> us-east -> eu).
Ryan: Scheduling 24h run now. Will rerun stress loops and production shadow for 1h every 6h.
Sanjay: Excellent. If the 24h remains clean, we proceed with staged rollout and a 1% canary in prod per region for 3 hours each stage.
Emily: I'll reserve extra capacity and update the on-call rota for the rollout night.
Sanjay: Thanks all — next update when 24h complete. :thumbsup:
